audits.title: Prospective Audit of Hand-Scrubbing Practices in an Orthopedic Operating Theatre in a Regional Headquarter Hospital of Northern Pakistan
audits.setting: Orthopaedic operating theatre, Regional Headquarter Hospital Skardu

cycle1.result: Scrub duration at least two minutes 45%, coverage of all surfaces 50%, proper antiseptic use 60%, correct drying 55%, overall aseptic protocol 70% (about 40 staff)

audits.intervention: Live demonstrations of correct hand scrubbing and visual reminder posters in the scrub area

cycle2.result: Scrub duration 90%, coverage 88%, antiseptic use 93%, drying 87%, overall aseptic protocol 95%; all improvements statistically significant

audits.citation: Rehman S, Rathore Z, Mehdivi MA, Hussain N, Uroosh L. Prospective Audit of Hand-Scrubbing Practices in an Orthopedic Operating Theatre in a Regional Headquarter Hospital of Northern Pakistan. . 2026. doi:10.64898/2026.03.14.26348091.

audits.title: Achieving Perfect Hand Washing: an Audit Cycle with Surgical Internees.
audits.standard: Ideal surgical hand washing technique; target 100% compliance
audits.setting: Tertiary care hospital (RG Kar Medical College and Hospital), Kolkata
audits.intervention: Video demonstration, personal demonstration by a consultant and individual instruction over repeated attempts.
audits.other_findings: Personal instruction was the most effective intervention; hand washing technique needed the most attempts (6) to correct.
audits.citation: Mukherjee R, Roy P, Parik M. Achieving Perfect Hand Washing: an Audit Cycle with Surgical Internees. Indian J Surg. 2021;83(5):1166-1172. doi:10.1007/s12262-020-02619-8. PMID: 33041566.

audits.title: Improving Quality and Compliance of Surgical Hand Scrubbing Practices: A Clinical Audit.
audits.setting: Operating theatres, Osman Degna (Prince Othman Digna) Teaching Hospital, Port Sudan
audits.intervention: Video demonstrations, hands-on training and feedback
audits.other_findings: Largest gain (51.5%) in rotational rubbing with clasped fingers; palms and rinsing improved by 30.3-42%.

audits.title: Surgical Hand Scrubbing: A Clinical Audit at a Referral Hospital.
audits.setting: Operating theatres, Prince Osman Digna Referral Hospital

cycle1.result: Baseline compliance (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Instructional videos, practical training sessions and direct feedback, reinforced with live demonstrations

cycle2.result: Compliance rose from 82% to 96% between the last two cycles; drying with a sterile towel improved from 30% to 42.8%.

audits.other_findings: Three cycles of 30 observations; scrubbing for a minimum of two minutes rose by 166%.
audits.citation: Ahmed EAO, Mohamed ZHS, Sayed MS, Mohamed Ahmed EA, Bala AMAA, Abdelrahem MA, et al.. Surgical Hand Scrubbing: A Clinical Audit at a Referral Hospital. Cureus. 2025;17(11):e96465. doi:10.7759/cureus.96465. PMID: 41393543.

audits.title: Improving Compliance With Surgical Scrubbing and Sterilization Protocols: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project at Atbara Teaching Hospital.
audits.standard: 27 criteria from international infection prevention guidelines across five domains
audits.setting: Operating theatre complex, Atbara Teaching Hospital

cycle1.result: Head cover 47.7%; scrubbing before gowning or gloving 50.0%; correct gowning 44.4%; anaesthetist hand hygiene 22.2%; correct sterile opening sequence 44.4%.

audits.intervention: Education, audit feedback, visual reminders and multidisciplinary engagement.

cycle2.result: Head cover 70.7%; scrubbing 88.2%; gowning 91.3%; anaesthetist hand hygiene 69.6%; sterile opening sequence 95.7% (all domains p<0.05).

audits.citation: Osman AMM, Mustafa SMB, Mahmoud AAO, Kubashi BMS, Ahmed MAY, Mohamed AMA, et al.. Improving Compliance With Surgical Scrubbing and Sterilization Protocols: A Two-Cycle Quality Improvement Project at Atbara Teaching Hospital. Cureus. 2026;18(7):e112559. doi:10.7759/cureus.112559. PMID: 42592220.
